lead: Connecticut homes are older than most, and more than a third still heat with oil. SootMend helps homes and businesses from Hartford to New Haven and Stamford recover from fire, smoke and soot.
risk: oil furnace puff-backs, heating and chimney fires in older homes, and kitchen fires
why: About 35% of Connecticut homes heat with fuel oil, one of the highest shares in the country. When an oil burner misfires, it can blow a puff-back of oily soot through ducts and into every room. Puff-backs are among the most common fire-related calls here, and they need very different cleaning from dry soot.

Much of Connecticut's housing is old, with colonials, capes and multi-family homes built long before modern codes. Fireplaces, wood stoves and old wiring are common. Hartford, New Haven, Bridgeport and Waterbury have many three-family homes where one fire affects several households.
problems: Hartford, New Haven, Bridgeport and Waterbury
tips: Have the oil burner cleaned and tuned every year before heating season.
If you hear a bang from the furnace or see black smudges at registers, shut it off and call for service.
Get chimneys swept before the first fire of the season.
Make sure every floor of a multi-family home has working smoke alarms.
insurance: Many Connecticut policies cover sudden puff-back damage, but some limit it, so ask your agent how your policy treats a puff-back before winter.
areas: Hartford, New Haven, Bridgeport, Stamford, Waterbury, Norwalk and small towns statewide are all covered.

faq.q: Is a furnace puff-back covered by insurance?
faq.a: Often, yes, when it is sudden and accidental. Many policies name it specifically. Shut the furnace off, photograph the soot, keep children and pets away and call your insurer before cleaning.
